app_answers.answer: Manage production in factories with many humans

app_answers.question: How long have each of you been working on this? How much of that has been full-time? Please explain.
app_answers.answer:
We have started working on this project in September 2020 and originally intended to use computer vision to count pallets produced in these factories. 

We realized this was not feasible because of GDPR and replaced cameras with RFID for counting productivity. We also realized there was a much bigger opportunity to become a platform for managing the entire production process (especially when there are many humans doing the work) and pivoted into the complete production management platform which we sell now.

We worked on it part time (~30 hours per week) from September 2020 to June 2021 and have both been full time since then.

app_answers.question: What is your company going to make? Please describe your product and what it does or will do.
app_answers.answer:
We have built a platform to track, manage and improve each step of the industrial production process for factories that are human labour intensive.

We developed touchscreen devices installed at each work area on the factory floor. Workers use RFID tags and touchscreens to create data events for when each unit is produced and when there are downtimes. Factory managers get real-time notifications of downtimes and when productivity is lower than expected so they can quickly act to improve productivity.

Our platform creates structured data around each step of the production process:
* receiving raw materials and completing preparation checklists 
* sending work to a workstation and monitoring its progress
* capturing quality control photographs (with automated AI inspection)
* confirming output counts
* generating invoices 
* clients can log in to view progress and quality control photographs

There are several stakeholders (worker, foreman, manager, external labour company, end client) and each has their own dashboard, automated alerts and data permissions. We create a history of every action taken on an order and enable the stakeholders to communicate in a single place with per-second manhours measurements per unit and detailed downtime data providing context. 

Communication between stakeholders is especially complicated and messy without our platform when the workers in the factory are contracted from an external labour provider as is the case in surprisingly many factories.

We have also developed a novel computer vision inspection system that is currently being piloted to generate per-unit quality metrics and generate a visual audit trail of each unit produced.

launches.body:
**TL;DR** We’re building this -

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79034&key=user_uploads/509746/b2c4bca3-62a5-4591-9743-29683d930076)

And we are Ex-Google and Meta robotics engineers that are using foundation vision models to solve the riddle of high-mix to redefine American manufacturing.

—

### **🚨 The Problem:**

U.S. manufacturing is making a comeback for the first time since the 1970s, but there is a problem: **Nobody is filling these jobs**. Decades of decline and entire generations shying away from manufacturing jobs have left the industry facing an expected 2.4 million jobs going unfulfilled by 2030. 

The obvious solution is to use robots, but **75% of all U.S. manufacturers are effectively unable to use traditional robotic automation** due to their high-mix production: they produce a wide array of products in small quantities. Traditional automation is rigid and needs new fixturing and re-programming for each part, and doesn’t provide ROI for high-mix manufacturers since so little of each part is produced. 

If America is unable to capitalize on the current manufacturing and AI boom, we lose out on **$1 trillion per year in opportunity cost** and the chance to strengthen our weakened industrial base. High-mix manufacturers are a crucial component for this and they urgently need adaptable automation solutions that can cheaply handle their large variety of parts. 

### **🦾 Our Solution:**

Pivot Robotics combines off-the-shelf robots and vision sensors with our pioneering AI vision control software to give industrial robots the ability to adapt. Our first product, Proteus, addresses the dangerous and unpopular task of grinding metal parts, offering zero-shot adaptation to new parts with the same precision, and efficiency. **We do this by leveraging the latest advances in foundational vision models**, allowing us to avoid the large data requirements that prior attempts of adding vision to industrial robots faced. We are currently engaged in a **pilot to deploy 10+ Proteus systems** at a large cast iron foundry that produces over 200 different parts a year.

### **🤝 Who We Are:**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79034&key=user_uploads/509746/dca22c09-4fc2-4c3c-aa64-5482d6880583)

We both met on the first day of college at Carnegie Mellon University, living 2 doors across from each other. 

[Siddharth](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/1333819/linkedin_redirect?key=74798b374abfa1117de67acaa6e2c7591293097d) has worked on self-driving cars at Uber ATG, AI at Meta, and most recently was designing multi-agent algorithms for warehouse robots at Nimble Robotics.

[Vignesh](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/509746/linkedin_redirect?key=102ec6e610057e9a5088e60101031188a7145ab9) optimized motion planning for general-purpose robots at Google X, researched LLM applications for robotics in the Atkeson Lab, and worked on manipulation at ABB.

Both of us are inspired to use our robotics experience to solve real-world labor problems after watching our respective parents’ careers in these industries (agriculture and manufacturing).

### 🔮**The Future:**

Expanding our vision technology to develop hand-eye coordination for robot arms, enabling the automation of tasks beyond grinding, like materials handling and assembly for high-mix manufacturers.

### **🙏Our Ask:**

We’re looking for introductions to manufacturing partners eager to embrace AI-driven automation and investors who share our vision for the future of manufacturing.

### **✉️ Contact Us:**

Reach out at [founders@pivotrobotics.com](mailto:founders@pivotrobots.com) and follow us on [Twitter](https://twitter.com/pivotrobots)/[Linkedin](https://www.linkedin.com/company/pivot-robots/) for updates and cool demos.

launches.body:
**_TL;DR_**: Ultra robots automate e-commerce order packaging and returns in fulfillment centers. Traditional automation isn't working for warehouses because it's costly, rigid, and often underutilized. Our robots are different: they’re easy to deploy, resilient to changing environments, and powered by AI that’s trained with examples.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=83218&key=user_uploads/36827/b95e65a5-16bd-4a49-9790-0cf80c5b5c27)

Hi everyone - we’re [Oliver](https://www.linkedin.com/in/oliverortlieb/), [Chetan,](https://www.linkedin.com/in/chetan-parthiban/) [Jon](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jmschwartz11/), and [Max](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mfriefeld/). After years of building and scaling manufacturing and robotics companies (_Layer By Layer, S13, and Voodoo Manufacturing, W17_), we’re now focused on bringing automation to the industries that need it most.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=83218&key=user_uploads/36827/8b8174a9-9ca6-46cc-b6f6-f7b1e854c160)

We believe we’re at a moment in history when robots can be made accessible and capable enough for mass adoption - and we need it more than ever.

**Labor is harder to come by than it’s been in decades**.

Imagine running a warehouse: you hire 20 temp workers to come in one day, but only 15 show up in the morning, and just 5 return after lunch. That’s the reality one of our partners told us they face.

In 2018, the U.S. entered its first labor shortage in over 60 years. Today, we are short over 1.3 million workers, causing companies to go understaffed or rely on high-churn temp labor.

And yet, **traditional warehouse automation isn’t being adopted fast enough**.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=83218&key=user_uploads/36827/04cde5a1-5136-4f3b-b880-24464506183b)

# **🤖 Ultrabots**

Ultra is building robots that can be dropped in at existing workstations and quickly trained to do repetitive tasks. They are more cost-effective than human labor and can operate around the clock, giving your team [✨](https://emojipedia.org/sparkles)superpowers[✨.](https://emojipedia.org/sparkles)

We use reliable off-the-shelf hardware so we can focus on rapid deployment. The key to unlocking the next million robots is data scale, and the fastest way to get there is to put robots in real-world environments doing useful tasks.

# **⏰ Why Now?**

Recent AI breakthroughs mean we can control robots with neural nets trained with examples, rather than with explicitly programmed routines.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=83218&key=user_uploads/36827/ebd67a19-babf-4f49-81f4-7994950ed7f7)

_Above is an example of a fully autonomous picking policy we trained on \~2hrs of data from teleoperating our research arms. The two RGB camera feeds are the input to the model, which outputs the joint+gripper positions at 10Hz._

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=83218&key=user_uploads/36827/13ced136-d5de-4a57-ade8-cb53e074a4a7)

_Examples of emergent behavior learned from the training data, but not explicitly programmed like what would be required in traditional automation._

# **🙏 Asks**

We’d love to connect to e-commerce 3PLs and large brands that handle their own fulfillment. You can reach us at [founders@ultra.tech](mailto:founders@ultra.tech). Thanks!

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=83257&key=user_uploads/1087615/dea0086b-00cd-4322-b4ba-d670c17a85f8)

Hello, we’re Alex and Devan, and we’re building the low-cost cruise missiles the United States needs!

**What we’re building**

Ares is building a new class of anti-ship cruise missiles. We are going to deliver the capabilities that the DoD wants in a form factor that’s 10x smaller and 10x cheaper.

Our missiles will be compatible with existing launch platforms, deliver smaller payloads at high subsonic speeds, and take out ships hundreds of miles away. We’re focusing on ground and ship-launched variants to start but will expand into air-launched versions, as well as versions with extended ranges and different payloads.

**Why we’re doing this**

A war with China in the Taiwan Strait would look nothing like what we've seen in Ukraine or the Middle East. Wargames within DoD and military experts are in agreement that the most useful weapons in such a conflict would be long range anti-ship weapons or cruise missiles.

The United States is not adequately prepared. In a potential conflict, our stockpiles will run out in weeks, and we currently don’t have the industrial capacity to build at a rate that could win a war, much less deter China. Higher-ups in DoD are waking up to the problem, and generals such as Major General Cameron Holt and officials such as Chairman of the House Select Committee on China Mike Gallagher have echoed this sentiment.

Recent conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine have shown that our weapons are too large, too expensive for the wars of today. Existing anti-ship cruise missiles are low-volume, multi-million dollar, 3,000 lb behemoths meant to take out large cruisers and destroyers.

But Chinese shipbuilding capability is far superior to ours, and we can’t make enough anti-ship missiles to counter. In addition, huge missiles aren’t needed to take out the smaller corvettes and frigates that make up the People’s Liberation Army Navy. And $3M missiles make even less sense to take out swarms of $200k small, unmanned surface vessels.

The DoD needs smaller, less expensive cruise missiles, and lots of them! But no one has delivered on that promise yet.

**How we know how to do this**

Both of us have worked at multiple defense and munitions startups. [Devan](https://www.linkedin.com/in/devanplantamura) is an Army Psychological Operations and Navy combat veteran and has deep experience in operations and business development at well-funded defense startups. [Alex](https://www.linkedin.com/in/alextseng1/) was the first engineering hire at an earlier missile startup, built autonomous systems at Rivian and Stanford, and worked on turbojets at CSULB.

**Where we’re at now**

We spent the summer building multiple prototypes and flight-testing them in the Mojave. In 11 weeks, we went from starting the company to flight testing with our own design. We are on track to deliver early working missile systems to our first customers by mid-2025.

We believe our vision for anti-ship cruise missiles can help fill the munitions gap that the US faces. At Ares, we would never wish for a war to occur. But by helping to rebuild our defense industrial base, we can make sure the United States is prepared to stop a conflict and save countless lives.

**Our Ask**

We are looking for extremely talented aerospace engineers to help bring our prototypes to fruition. If you know any aerodynamics, propulsion, or GNC engineers who are interested in building something incredibly cool and want to make a positive difference in geopolitics, please send them our way!

Even the most data-savvy teams can’t keep up, leaving owners with little visibility into how others are making money. And rule changes aren’t just small tweaks – they can completely upend the market. To avoid financial penalties, battery owners spend millions on lawyers and consultants just to stay compliant.

Dartboard is an AI Analyst that uncovers missed revenue for owners of grid connected batteries while ensuring compliance. We provide value in two key ways:

* **Market Intelligence:** We ingest historical market data so that owners can evaluate optimization strategies and uncover money they might be leaving on the table.
* **Regulatory Guidance:** Our AI Analyst, trained on the latest rule changes, translates complex regulations into clear, actionable insights — helping owners navigate compliance without the need for expensive consultants.

The wholesale distribution industry is massive: _$9T+ in annual revenue. 410,000+ businesses. 6 million+ employees._

  (“Most of my sales reps are **retiring in the next 2-3 years**, I have **NO idea** what I’ll do after” - a medium sized electrical goods distributor from Indiana we met)
* **Reps spend less than 30% of their time selling**. The rest? Answering repetitive calls (“What’s the price of this SKU?” “Which warehouse has it?”), digging through systems, and manual follow-ups.
* **Over 25% of inbound calls never reach a human** — lost revenue, lost trust, lost time.

This isn’t just inefficiency. It’s operational drag at scale — and it's only getting worse.

[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s1NVVxRnLL8](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s1NVVxRnLL8%5C%5C)

We’re building Kanava AI, a voice-based AI agent designed for wholesale distributors.

Most AI tools in this space fail because they try to do too much, too early, and distributors are famously late adopters. We’re taking a more deliberate path: start with low-leverage work, prove value, and scale responsibility as the system earns it.

launches.tagline: Your next lunar mission just got easier!
launches.body:
# tl;dr

Cascade Space is building a turn-key communications system for lunar and deep space missions. Our ground station network and integrated software tools work together to maximize uptime and availability, while reducing spacecraft iteration cycles from weeks to hours. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=90423&key=user_uploads/222992/7b3a56ce-8dc0-48db-a2e5-3badb2afd893)

**Why are we building this and why now?**

The Deep Space Network (DSN), NASA’s global network of ground terminals for communicating with deep space probes, is [oversubscribed by 40% and in desperate need of upgrades.](https://newspaceeconomy.ca/2024/09/02/nasas-deep-space-network-challenges-and-the-road-ahead/) The DSN is all but unavailable for most commercial operations. Companies with missions going to the Moon and beyond have to deal with a patchwork of individual dish operators for every mission, each with bespoke hardware, specs, and interfaces. Furthermore, many of these commercial providers are not able to handle the demand and [operational failures also can lead to loss of mission](https://www.astroforge.com/updates-collection/odint-mission-debrief).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=90423&key=user_uploads/222992/c6aa8968-e567-42e5-8866-866414630f22)

**Comms system design is fraught with peril**

The spacecraft comms system design is tightly coupled to the available ground network. Engineers spend hundreds of hours poring over datasheets, on the phone with vendors and suppliers, and endless email threads, only to put all this data into a giant spreadsheet to make sense of it. Every iteration requires not only painful attention to detail, but also in-depth esoteric knowledge of how radio frequency systems and channel coding schemes work in order to accurately predict in-flight performance. Simple misunderstandings can lead to catastrophic errors in design and configuration.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=90423&key=user_uploads/222992/1623d16f-4789-4793-892f-2c7adffc84a7)

**End-to-end comms system validation often doesn’t happen**

Fully integrated testing between the spacecraft and ground terminal is typically cost prohibitive. Instead, engineers compare spec sheets and email configurations to the ground operators, and hope it works in flight (spoiler alert: it often doesn’t). It is routine for spacecraft to fly having never done an end-to-end test of their system with ground terminal representative hardware. The whole process is subject to human error from end to end. 

**This approach to space communications does not scale**

Commercial space ventures beyond low earth orbit have already pushed existing infrastructure to its breaking point, and demand for deep space comms support is expected to grow exponentially over the next decade. We will not have a spacefaring future for humanity until communications for spacecraft become as easy as signing up for cable internet. 

**We are redefining the process, starting with spacecraft design**

Better comms starts at the beginning, in the early trade study and design phase. We are replacing industry-standard spreadsheets with a modern software tool that lets you see how your system will perform with our ground network in real time.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=90423&key=user_uploads/222992/4873c5a0-9288-48fe-8d2e-a3a32f3fcad0)

**Test as you fly, fly as you test**

You don’t rise to the level of your expectations, you fall to the level of your testing. We ship you a “ground station in a box,” identical to hardware we’ve installed at the ground stations you will be using, and provide you with a test plan that you can use to test your entire system end to end, with both the space vehicle and the ground terminal in the loop. 

**Launch with confidence**

Fly and operate your spacecraft. Use our API to schedule passes on our network, track your spacecraft, stream data, monitor the ground site, and access recordings.

launches.body:
# **What is F4 in a nutshell?**

We’re helping hardware-rich teams 10x how they redline and interpret engineering GD&T drawings. With backgrounds at Tesla and SpaceX, we’re building a platform that finally treats drawings like code—automatically validating every dimension, tolerance, and GD&T symbol against standards so noncompliance is caught instantly.

https://youtu.be/SYzqZ4XWmCA

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=93123&key=user_uploads/2642473/a6d6c66e-7e58-4405-b4e2-48c30b354495)

# **The Problem & Why We Built F4**

Drawing literacy is one of the weakest skills across hardware teams. Yet drawings are made every day.

These aren’t just illustrations—they’re effectively business contracts between designers and manufacturers, defining what’s acceptable in production. Drawings carry the bulk of design intent—fit, form, function, and fabrication—and act as the important source of truth across production, quality, and supply chain.

GD&T standards from ASME and ISO exist to formalize this communication. But they’re dense and confusing. Across major revision years, there are thousands of pages of definitions, edge cases, and revision quirks. Designers are expected to know it all, leads are expected to catch every mistake, and suppliers are expected to interpret drawings flawlessly. One mistake means scrap, delays, or worse.

# **Our Solution**

Why is something so critical still so manual? Why can’t drawings be validated and interpreted more quickly and robustly —like code? Why can’t hardware dev be more like software dev?

We’re changing exactly that!

F4 treats drawings like code—they either execute or fail immediately. Our platform checks every dimension, tolerance, and GD&T symbol against standards in real-time, ensuring full compliance before a drawing ever reaches the floor. No more total reliance on manual redlining and reviews.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=93123&key=user_uploads/2642473/1aa5904c-3086-4722-8838-ffda9c0d7a85)

F4 ensures engineers never release noncompliant drawings—and suppliers never misinterpret them. F4 helps industrial teams eliminate costly scrap, rework, and miscommunication at the root.

# **How It Works**

1. Upload a drawing (dxf…and very soon pdf)
2. Select GD&T standard of choice (ASME Y14.5 - 1994, 2009, & 2018)
3. Get instant compliance score graded against a desired GD&T standard using **deterministic logic**
4. Get recommendation to correct any asset (FCF, FOS, datum, basic, modifier, and/or dimension) of the drawing that is noncompliant with references to ground-truth sources
5. With a compliant drawing - get standard definition, inspection plan, and tolerance analysis interpretations on any drawing asset of interest

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=93123&key=user_uploads/2642473/accc67da-db20-423d-84b0-7ec4904ad800)

## **Hardware Platform Built by Hardware Engineers!**

I worked at Tesla as a Mechanical Design Engineer and took 6 parts from clean sheet design to production for the CyberCab and SEMI drive system programs. I was also the lead engineer for Tesla’s global drive unit heat exchanger program with +3 million unit annual production volume.

Aidan worked at SpaceX as an Avionics Test Engineer, where he designed and owned testing hardware (PCB boards and testing apparatus) for the Raptor 3 Engine - the most advanced rocket engine in the world. 

In college, we led The University of Alabama’s Rocket Team where we achieved the university’s first-ever liquid rocket engine hotfire! I built the rocket engine and Aidan built the electrical/software for our propulsion system.

Robotic factories building robots. Today we have a 12,000 sqft factory in the Bay Area manufacturing everything from full humanoids to robots for the International Space Station.

Our thesis: Revitalizing domestic manufacturing means driving costs down through automation. We are building an autonomous factory that is able to autonomously process a new order end to end from prototyping to large batch production. That means supply chain management, design for manufacturing, industrial machine retooling, robotic adaptation, quality inspection, packaging, and logistics all automated. Goal: Create a factory that can autonomously go from placed customer order to completed unit scale manufacturing run in 24 hours.

We are currently manufacturing production runs from top labs, full humanoids, and even have a partnership to manufacture robotics for the International Space Station. We've also built supply chain relationships in electronics, actuators, SMT, computing, pneumatics, and raw material suppliers.

A snippet of some of our machines in the factory:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112228&key=user_uploads/2763027/777065e0-e83d-4501-8799-8c490e883851)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112228&key=user_uploads/2763027/30775e59-e171-4949-b959-3dc06ffa5322)

## **Manufacturing at the Core**

This isn't just a robotic manipulation company. Its a manufacturing company.

Internally we have pipelines autonomous building large databases of actuators, and raw tracking and trying to predict what items will need to order now to meet our next day targets.

## **The Harness**

The entire factory is a data harness we can "backprop" learnings through from errors in the customer designs, failed supply chain prediction, slow retoolings, to inaccurate robotic manipulation. Our core belief is that robotic machine learning should not rely on human data to scale but instead learn to improve from its own mistakes in the real world in real time. This closes the manufacturing data gap that currently limits large-scale factory automation.

On a personal note, not only do I believe we have the opportunity to build a great business but also to make a positive impact on the world. Lets build a better world :)

Factories need to be designed from the ground up _around_ robots, not the other way around.

launches.body:
Hey everyone, we’re [Eoin ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/eoincobbe)and [Robert](https://www.linkedin.com/in/robert-cormican-a4405990), co-founders of Forge Robotics.

We are completely changing the way that metal fabrication is done. Companies can no longer afford to deal with massive labour shortages and rising costs of outdated processes. Forge is on the journey to enable companies to take in raw stock metal and output completed metal parts without human intervention.

# TL;DR

Forge is building a system that turns dumb, human-programmed industrial welding robot arms into autonomous members of the workforce.

From here, we will deliver autonomous factory units that handle all processes in metal fabrication, from handling cut parts and positioning them for assembly, to welding and cleaning up final assemblies.

To get involved, contact us @ [eoin@forge-robotics.com](https://eoin@forge-robotics.com)

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5vxp75bUlIY&t=38s

# 🏭 The Problem

Manufacturing is an industry that has been all but left behind for the past 20 years compared to the advances in software development, self-driving vehicles, and all other fields that AI has revolutionised.

**Labour shortages**

Manufacturing of defence equipment, construction machines, and automotive make up the backbone of much of the American economy. In the U.S, there are 400,000 unfilled welding positions, and that is expected to rise to 600,000 by 2030.

**Push to reshore**

OEMs and Tier 1 manufacturers are pushing to reshore their manufacturing, but traditional methods of operation mean that they are failing to operate profitably when competing with manufacturing in offshore economies.

**Failure of current automation**

Current industrial robots can only achieve a very narrow set of well-defined manufacturing tasks because of the way robots are programmed. Traditionally programmed welding robots end up with around 10% of parts needing rework due to the delta in geometry from part to part.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=95362&key=user_uploads/2795202/eb13105f-47fa-4312-b8c7-185ecac7e04a)

# 🦾 Our solution

Forge provides a vision system and robotic intelligence that creates a sub-mm map, identifies all features and weld seams, and autonomously controls the welding robot arms.

Metal fabrication companies will now:

* No longer have to **manually program** robotic arms
* Achieve **99% first pass line yield**, up from the current 90%
* Use robotic welding arms in many previously infeasible situations

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=95362&key=user_uploads/2795202/82ef4c04-835c-4a20-a6b6-85698177d54b)

# ♾️ Fully autonomous production

Using the manufacturing intelligence system that we are working on for factories today, we will be delivering fully autonomous modular factory units that handle all of the metal manufacturing processes to take raw steel parts to finished welded assemblies. Saving companies **Tens of millions** per year by changing the way they manufacture.

# 🤝 Ask

Can you introduce us to companies in the metal manufacturing industry? We are currently taking on as many pilot customers as we can!

If this is a future that excites you and you want to find out how you can be part of it 👉Contact Eoin @ [eoin@forge-robotics.com](https://eoin@forge-robotics.com)

Find out more @ [www.forge-robotics.com](https://forge-robotics.com/)

**TLDR:** Drones and robotics are driving demand for high-performance materials at an all-time high. We make it easier to manufacture aerospace-grade carbon fiber parts thanks to our bespoke 5-axis manufacturing cell.

https://youtu.be/9H3dZBSVojE

Hey all,

We are [Giuseppe](https://x.com/peps_rp) and [Rollo](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rollo-tully-5a3306221/),

We started with manufacturing UAVs together back in university, and now we are creating a manufacturing cell to make better composite parts for aerospace and robotics.

**Why work on this?**

Conventional composites manufacturing faces long lead times (2-10 weeks)

This is how the standard process looks like:

1\.     Mold manufacturing (1-4 weeks, $10k–$100k+).

2\.     Manual layup (8-40 labor hours @ 30-80$/hr).

3\.     Part curing (3-20hr, autoclave CAPEX: $35k-$500k+).

4\.     Post-processing (2-5 days).

One design iteration burns weeks and money; a small design change results in going back to step 1.

Engineering teams need faster lead times, lower barriers to entry for manufacturing, and more design freedom.

**The solution**

We condense all of those steps in a single manufacturing cell, producing parts in a day instead of weeks, offering unprecedented design opportunities.

Our MK1 custom manufacturing cell is equipped with:

* 5 degrees of freedom for non-planar operations
* thermal chamber for high-performance materials
* switchable end effectors for additive and subtractive manufacturing of composites
* 1.5m tall build chamber for large structures production

Our software stack is the first optimized 5-axis slicer for continuous fiber that can deposit material along the stress fields direction of the component, which allows us to produce parts as strong as metals but as light as plastics.

We engineer and produce our own reinforced thermoplastic stock in-house. We believe that material science advancements lie at the base of most significant step changes in the progress of a civilization, and our fundamental belief is that we have barely scratched the surface of what these materials can achieve.

launches.body:
<https://youtu.be/DfSQ8L7d0BM?si=9Zp7BVPvCD_vB4ke>\
\
**THE PROBLEM**

Industrial control software still looks and feels like it was built in the Windows 95 era. Manufacturers spend weeks stitching together Programable Logic Controllers (PLCs), Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA), HMIs, databases, and custom integrations just to get systems running. Additionally, legacy systems collect enormous amounts of high-quality data, but don’t do _anything_ with it, even though it could easily be used for things such as anomaly detection or optimization recommendations.\
\
**OUR SOLUTION**

We're building an AI-native platform to unify the industrial control stack, starting with SCADA and eventually extending down to PLC hardware and the devices on the factory floor. We offer both a product and a service:

**1) Software**

We already built a full SCADA system to replace legacy platforms like Ignition, WinCC, and FactoryTalk. It’s AI native: users can use AI to generate controls screens in seconds (this used to take hours), write custom scrips/logical flows, and automatically detect issues before they become catastrophic. \
\
Not only is this a full SCADA system, but it can operate on top of an existing one so that users can take advantage of our “intelligence layer” without having to rip out their current infrastructure (people understandably don’t like doing this).\
\
**2) System Integration** 

We’ve recently expanded to become an AI-native industrial integrator. Instead of just selling our software, we integrate it into our clients existing stack for them, and help them set up any other tools they need to run it. 

Over the past few months, we've spent hundreds of hours talking with controls engineers, manufacturers, operators, and system integrators. We already knew that industrial software was broken, but we also learned that even when better technology exists, people are understandably cautious about adopting it. These systems run critical infrastructure and reliability matters more than novelty. Change is slow, but we want to reindustrialize America now.

**Instead of waiting for the industry to adopt an entirely new software stack, we're bringing our technology directly into customer projects today.**

While larger firms can spend millions on integration services, smaller firms don’t have that kind of money. Traditional integrators use highly manual methods to set up their clients software stacks (which are also outdated). By leveraging AI, we’ll be able to set up the same systems at 10x the speed and charge way less. 

**Our ask: if you’re exploring controls/automation systems, PLC programming, SCADA systems, or system integration**, **we’d love to talk. Or, if you know any deep tech companies that want to set up a controls system, let us know!**

See more at <https://controlseat.com>.

**Hey everyone 👋**

I'm Justin, founder of Sidekick.

**TL;DR** Sidekick is an AI assistant that frontline manufacturing workers use over text message. They text a number and it answers from the company's own documents, creates and routes work orders, and syncs with the software the company already uses. No app, no login, no training. I built Sidekick for my dad's manufacturing shop. It’s now live at facilities across the globe.

**_Ask:_** Do you know anyone who owns or runs a manufacturing plant, warehouse, or industrial facility? I'd love an intro! Email [**justin@textsidekick.com**](mailto:justin@textsidekick.com) or [**book a demo**](https://calendly.com/justin-textsidekick).

Check out our launch video:

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yxwq5ZAojXg>

## ❌ The Problem

I grew up in my dad's manufacturing plants and spent summers working on the factory floor at EDS Manufacturing.

Here's what I watched happen repeatedly. A machine goes down, everyone's waiting, and the person who can help is in a meeting or on another line. Half the time the answer already existed. Nobody could get to it.

Why it keeps happening:

* **No computer access.** Nobody on that floor has a company login or an email address, so none of the plant's software reaches them.
* **The answers are scattered.** An SOP in a binder, a manual on a shared drive few have permissions to, a safety procedure someone printed and taped to a wall in 2019.
* **The best answers were never written down.** Thirty years of tribal knowledge lives in one guy's head, and when he retires it leaves with him.
* **So the same questions get asked over and over.** Shift after shift, and every one of them costs somebody their afternoon.

There are 239,000 manufacturing plants in the US, and only 29% of the people working in them have advanced digital skills. Any tool that requires a download, a login, and training makes adoption difficult.

## ✅ Our Solution

Workers text the Sidekick phone number. Problems, photos, voice memos, in any language. No app to download, no account to create, nothing to learn. Every worker on the floor already knows how to send a text, which is why adoption isn't a fight.

* **Answers from your own documents.** SOPs, manuals, safety procedures, tribal knowledge. Sidekick responds in the worker's language, in seconds.
* **Creates and routes the work order.** The issue gets logged and sent to the right person, without anyone needing a laptop.
* **Syncs with the software you already run.** Sidekick pulls from and writes to your existing systems instead of replacing them, and integrates directly through PLC and SCADA systems so the floor and the software finally see the same thing.
* **Captures tribal knowledge.** Every exchange builds a searchable knowledge base the company owns, so the know-how stays when the veteran leaves.

Here's a full walkthrough:

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=a5zBRSXi-90>

## 👤 The Team

I'm Justin, founder and CEO. I'm the third generation in a manufacturing family, and I've been around plant floors since I was a kid. I studied Computer Science at the University of Pennsylvania, worked in finance at Arm, and left both to build Sidekick after watching the same problem play out on every floor I'd been on.

## 🙏 Our Ask

If you answer "yes" to any of these, I'd love your help:

* **Do you know anyone who owns or runs a manufacturing plant, warehouse, or industrial facility?** Even a name and a "you two should talk" goes a long way.
* **Have you sold software into manufacturing?** I'd love to hear what actually worked and what didn't.

Contact me at [**justin@textsidekick.com**](mailto:justin@textsidekick.com) or [**book a demo here**](https://calendly.com/justin-textsidekick)**.**

launches.tagline: Hera reviews every drawing against your factory's own standards and the ASME code, catching expensive mistakes and preventing rework 10x faster than manual review.
launches.body:
**TL;DR: Every custom metal part starts as a drawing, and every drawing gets checked by hand before anyone builds it. Hera does that check in minutes instead of a full day, and catches the mistakes that turn into scrapped parts.**

[**https://youtu.be/J_5NRjkou3Y**](https://youtu.be/J_5NRjkou3Y)

**The Problem**

Custom mechanical parts run on 2D drawings. Whether you're an OEM releasing drawings to suppliers, or an aerospace supplier answering to source inspection, every drawing has to be checked against ASME/ISO standards and GD&T requirements before it goes anywhere near a machine.

Right now, that review is done by hand, and usually by the most senior engineer in the building. And a single missed tolerance callout or an ambiguous datum reference can mean a scrapped part, a blown schedule, or a shipment that fails inspection.

We heard the same story from a pressure vessel fabricator, a semiconductor tooling shop, and a medical device manufacturer: reviews take days. This isn't because the work is hard. There's simply no good way to do it faster without cutting corners, and nobody cuts corners on a drawing that could scrap a $40,000 part.

**Our Solution**

Hera is a brain for manufacturing. Any real advance in manufacturing has to be grounded in two things: the standards parts are held to and the reality of the shop floor. So that's what we built Hera on.

Upload a drawing and Hera checks GD&T callouts, tolerance stack ups, and title block requirements against ASME Y14.5, relevant ISO standards, and your own design intent. The result is a drawing your shop can build right the first time, without the delays and rework that eat margins. Every review also makes Hera more valuable, creating a system of record for drawing errors that helps teams build better models for engineering processes.

**While the current review takes days, Hera takes minutes… and gets better by the drawing.**

**Us**

**Noelle** grew up in an industrial park her family runs in the Philippines and has been on factory floors her whole life. At 19, she built a water-treatment facility that added 40 L/s of capacity to the park. 

**Meera** has spent years around manufacturing: at her family's plants, and on projects at Pfizer and TE Connectivity, where she built a SOTA discrete-event simulation. She taught herself PLC programming and C++, and has published ML research at UW.

We actually met on a bus to a factory tour, and have been best friends ever since!

**TLDR:** Our software turns robots into independent survey and inspection workers at your facility.

[Launch Video](https://youtu.be/7xObOE6knZM)

## **Life and death pain worth $Millions/year**

At every nuclear facility, highly trained radiation-protection teams spend hours each day walking the site, filling out hand-drawn maps, and searching for something life-threatening: radiation. IN THE BEST CASE they find nothing, and still have to return to their posts to transcribe the data into a computer before doing the actual high-value work they were assigned. These surveys are time-consuming, dangerous, expensive, and prone to data inconsistencies that carry direct regulatory consequences.

The same pain exists well beyond nuclear. Whether it's gas-leak inspection or ammonia surveys, similar workflows run across oil, gas, chemical, biological, space, and other hazardous facilities.

## **What we do**

An operator defines the work from a simple dashboard; the robot then navigates the site, handles instruments, opens doors, turns valves, collects measurements, and generates structured, auditable, compliance-ready reports. We're hardware-agnostic, so plants run our software on robots they already own, many of which sit in a closet today as "$200k paperweights, " or we can provide the right robot for the job. Our stack is designed for safety-critical infrastructure and comes with theoretical safety guarantees, exactly what regulators and plant leadership require. Our core manipulation framework was not possible before and is based on **breakthrough founder research** published and presented at the most prestigious IEEE journals and conferences in the world. 

We're already in active contract-scoping conversations across the nuclear industry and oil & gas.

* Sites where routine surveys are frequent, hard to staff, or particularly painful? We'd love to hear about them.
